CONTINUE135 / #27 / arena/ef6b75ef: after 134 handoff 6439951448, read the **apply seed, the two backend writers' entries and the channel samplers** from original bytes.

`6b2ce8` (apply context builder: `x0`=animator, `x1`=playable, `x2`=source, `x3`=context out, `x4`=arg3), `6b6950` (commit gate), `6b2bdc` (backend select), `6b784c` (controller resolve), `6bd5c0`/`6be690` (the two writers, entry only), `6b6850`/`6b1538` (evaluate companion + chain walk), `6a99f0`/`6a98c4`/`6a99a4`/`6a9b90` (channel set/release), `3dfa9c`/`3d8614`/`518b40`/`6d788c` (resolvers), `6b7cf8`/`6c7060` (vector builders), `6da998`, `6b7c14`, `6bad24`/`6bba14`, `6bc968`.

**Result 1 — `+0x610` of 134 now has a definition.** It is the version key of the apply context: a rebuild happens only when `context[0] != animator[+0x610]`; `6b6950` mirrors the counter into `context[0x58]` after committing. Refresh and apply therefore agree on the same change token, and the full copy map of the ~0x90-byte context (`+0x08 … +0x88`) is tabulated in the report.

**Result 2 — the two writers do not build the same entry.** `6b2bdc` picks on the byte at `+0x5e5` (set → `6bd5c0`, clear → `6be690`). Both call `6bc968`, but with **fourth argument 1 vs 0**, and the second one runs a `6bde64` pre-pass when bit 0 of its flag is set. Their interiors are past the 0x800 cap and are **not** read.

**Result 3 — first honest change detection.** `6a99f0` is a `kind = [x0+8]` switch, kinds 5..11 through the jump table at `0x152614`; `6a98c4` stores a value and returns `cset ne` against the old word, then invokes a global hook `[[0x10e18a8]](0, old, new)`; `6a99a4` (kind `0x0b`) returns `old != new`.

**Corrections made this cycle:** `6b1538` is a tagged chain walk, not a simple resolver; the invalid-state zero ranges of `6b2ce8` were incomplete before; `ctx+0x84` is `-1` or a word of `[[[src+0x48][0]]+0x50]`, not the playable byte; the recovery tool labels `6bc968` depth 1 although its parent is a followed callee, so the artifact reports it under `follow_depth.level2`; `6c7060` is annotated only for its first `0x150` bytes.

Provenance `arena/ef6b75ef`, branch `arena/ef6b75ef-windwings-space-shooter-game-p`, code SHA `0ffd421bffa1ee8a77fb8bd676956b885dd38a74`, CI Verify **40509111057 success**, recovery run **40507430140** (source `53f6536dc`, evidence `52c664057`). Probe `reverse-engineering/raw/owner135/probe.json.gz` 11743 B `c11aedd5868e29ad9493b934ad0c57fb4ba7cda4dd0d0d3de4d79750854070dd`; artifact `datas/l3_ef6b75ef135_native_apply_seed.json.gz` **10434 B `5c6d7d85dceb25fc46b13a9d7d4d3f83f706b0979c9d7a76b4e25c3e3555b534`** pinned to probe + upstream 129 `217f8893…`/133 `73542233…`/134 `74cf1843…` + tool SHA; local **41 focused OK / 1981 full OK (348.939 s)**; receipts `reverse-engineering/raw/l3-ef6b75ef135-verification/`; report `docs/apk-analysis/135-ef6b75ef-native-apply-samplers.md`.

Honest note on the docs commit: the receipts commit `58cf84cc5` tripped an existing markdown-link test in `docs/HANDOFF_AI_TASKS.md` (a `](` sequence inside the hook notation), run **40510320595** = failure; the notation was rewritten in `c8865ea43`, no data or verifier byte changed.

Counts are countable from the raw, not estimated: 24 bodies (15 seeds + 9 followed), 9952 B, 177 control transfers (89 `bl`), 12 in-cluster calls, 20 deduplicated indirect sites from 42 raw `ldr→blr` rows, 203 field rows, 297 byte-checked facts, 0 strings, 3 bodies truncated.

**Static only, no execution, no synthetic object**, no class/type name, no runtime or readback claim; `ldp/stp` are not field rows; jump-table targets are not decoded.

Review requests: (1) is the `+0x610` version-key reading enough to close 134's open definition? (2) which writer should the next cycle read past the cap — `6bd5c0` or `6be690`? (3) should `6c7060` become its own cycle with a larger window? #27-full stays OPEN: dispatcher/owner class, heap, scheduling, clip/clock writer, pose/blend/apply, readback/render.
